extracted.intended_audience: sceptical philosophers and mathematicians; educated readers of natural theology/natural philosophy
extracted.subtask_description: Constructing and evaluating arguments for the existence and attributes of God from observed laws of motion, gravity, and other mechanical phenomena (using experiments, celestial observations, and mathematical demonstration).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground arguments in experiment and experience
rubrics_metrics.description: being taught by sure Experiments, and by this mere and simple Gravity ... I shall therefore only endeavour to represent some few of those things that appear true by Experience
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use empirical observation and reproducible experiments as primary evidence. Prefer demonstrable phenomena (e.g., rivers, tides, projectile motion, planetary perturbations) rather than mere speculation. Anti-pattern: relying on unsupported opinion or untested hypothesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence from gravity's multiplicity of useful effects
rubrics_metrics.description: by this Gravity Rivers flow ... the Rains, Dew, &c. descend from the Clouds, and moisten the Earth ... Boats and Ships can sail upon Rivers and Seas ... innumerable other Uses, that are owing only to the Gravity of Water
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect and emphasize numerous practical and beneficial consequences of a physical law (here gravity) as evidence of purposeful ordering and goodness. Provide concrete examples (hydrology, navigation, pumps, fountains). Anti-pattern: ignoring the way regular laws produce widespread benefits when assessing design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish universality of the law (extension to heavens)
rubrics_metrics.description: this Natural Law of Gravity extends it self thro' the whole visible Universe, and seems to prevail over all, even over the great Heavenly Bodies, which gravitate towards each other in the same Manner as the sublunary Bodies
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show that the same law applies across scales (from water-particles to planets and satellites). Use observational astronomy and analogies between terrestrial and celestial mechanics. Example evidence: planetary orbits, satellite motion, mutual perturbations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use mathematical/geometrical demonstration of celestial motion
rubrics_metrics.description: the heavenly Bodies ... move about the Sun ... in a Curve Line ... an Ellipses ... a Planet being in any Point ... would pursue its Way according to the Right Lines ... and so would entirely forsake the said Curve Figure, which it describes, were it not that another Power did continually cause it to approach or incline towards the Sun
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use geometrical facts (tangent lines, ellipses) and mathematical reasoning to infer the existence and direction of forces (attractions). Present diagrams and show how deviations from inertial straight-line motion imply active forces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use observed perturbations as direct evidence of mutual attraction
rubrics_metrics.description: that besides this Gravitation or Attraction between the Planets and the Sun ... there may be visibly discovered the like Attraction between one Planet and the Satellites of another ... Saturn ... remained some Years ... about its Conjunction with Jupiter ... the Satellites of Jupiter do change their usual Course ... agreeable to the said Law of Attraction
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite specific observational cases where interactions (perturbations) between bodies produce measurable deviations from expected motion, and use those as direct support for mutual attraction. Example: Jupiter–Saturn conjunction effects on satellites. Anti-pattern: dismissing perturbations as noise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infer a non-material first cause from the nature of motion
rubrics_metrics.description: Motion does not belong to the Being of a Body. ... the first Cause thereof must be Incorporeal, and even wonderful and unconceivable in his Operations, forasmuch as not being a Body himself, he is able to move all Bodies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argue from the passivity of bodies (bodies are 'simple passive') and from the fact that motion can begin or cease that an immaterial (incorporeal) cause is required. Use philosophical premises about what constitutes a body and what belongs to essence vs. accident.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat the inertia axiom as a foundational mechanical premise
rubrics_metrics.description: A Body being once at Rest, or in Motion, ceases not from that Rest, or from being moved in a Right Line with the same Force, and without any Augmentation or Diminution thereof, unless another Force acting upon it produces a Change therein.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt the fundamental axiom of mechanics (inertia) as a starting point for inference. Use it to analyze whether continued motion requires continuous agency or can be fully explained by prior impulses. Note that this axiom is used to highlight puzzles about origin and continuance of motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use proportionality of causes and effects as analytic criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: That the Motions, and all their Differences and Changes in all Bodies are greater and smaller in Proportion, as the Powers which impress the same on those Bodies are greater or smaller.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the law of proportionality (effects scale with causes) to judge adequacy of proposed material causes. Use it to argue that minute initial impulses are inadequate to explain persistent large-scale motions without further cause. Anti-pattern: assuming disproportionate long-term effects follow from negligible initial causes without intermediate mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasize that communication and continuation of motion remain explanatorily obscure
rubrics_metrics.description: How the Motion of one Body is communicated or transferred to another? Which as far as I know, has never yet been rightly answered by any.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight unresolved explanatory gaps in mechanics (how motion is transmitted and sustained) and treat such gaps as grounds for positing an incomprehensible sustaining power. Antipattern: treating formal mechanical description as a complete ontological account without addressing this 'how'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infer wisdom/design from order, regularity, and fitness to human good
rubrics_metrics.description: among all the Events produced by Gravity, there are hardly any, or rather there are none at all, which do not contribute to his own, and all other Mens Happineſs, yet cannot see the Goodness and Mercy of God therein
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When natural laws produce widespread and beneficial effects (fit to human ends), use this teleological fit as evidence of a wise and benevolent designer. Provide many examples of beneficial regularities; anti-pattern: isolating harmful consequences while ignoring pervasive goods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject explanation by a series of ignorant/material causes for first cause
rubrics_metrics.description: There can be no ignorant necessary First Cause deduced from a Series of ignorant Causes operating together.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argue that chaining together material or 'ignorant' causes cannot yield a proper account of the first cause; the origin must be of a different, non-ignorant character. Anti-pattern: assuming aggregate material processes automatically supply ultimate explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use precise mechanical and mathematical phenomena (ballistics, catenary, fountains) as evidential exactness
rubrics_metrics.description: the Motion of the Parts of Gunpowder ... the discharge of Bullets from Guns ... they don't move one Point forwards without continually obeying the same ... fountains ... not one of them shall transgress the Line which the Mathematician can shew that it ought to describe ... the Catenaria or Chain-Line ... produced by the Gravity of the Parts of a Chain or Rope
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point to highly regular, mathematically describable behaviors in applied mechanics (ballistic trajectories, fountain streams, catenary curves) as evidence that nature obeys precise laws. Use demonstrations by great mathematicians (Leibnitz, Gregory) as supporting authority. Anti-pattern: treating approximate or qualitative regularity as equivalent to precise mathematical law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish necessity from contingency when inferring origins
rubrics_metrics.description: Can any Body likewise deduce these Principles from any Laws of Necessity, that is to say, from Laws that cannot be exerted otherwise, nor otherwise understood?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reasoning from observed regularities to origins, explicitly ask whether the observed regularities are necessary (could not be otherwise) or contingent (could have been different). Do not conflate empirical regularity with metaphysical necessity; use this distinction to justify inference to a non-necessary (free) first cause.
